definitions.explanation: A category of Japanese food made from fish paste (surimi) that is kneaded, shaped, and then steamed, grilled, or fried. Includes kamaboko, chikuwa, and other common items.

examples.japanese: おでんには{練|ね}り{物|もの}が{欠|か}かせない。
examples.english: Fish paste products are essential for oden.

examples.japanese: {練|ね}り{物|もの}コーナーで{竹輪|ちくわ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought chikuwa from the fish paste products section.

examples.japanese: この{地方|ちほう}は{新鮮|しんせん}な{魚|さかな}が{豊富|ほうふ}なので、{練|ね}り{物|もの}の{種類|しゅるい}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This region has abundant fresh fish, so there are many varieties of fish paste products.

notes:
Compound of {練|ね}る (to knead) and {物|もの} (thing/product). Refers to a broad category of processed fish foods central to Japanese cuisine.

TYPES:
- {蒲鉾|かまぼこ}: kamaboko — steamed fish cake, often with a pink outer layer
- {竹輪|ちくわ}: chikuwa — tube-shaped grilled fish cake
- さつま{揚|あ}げ: satsuma-age — deep-fried fish cake
- はんぺん: hanpen — soft, fluffy white fish cake
- {笹|ささ}かまぼこ: sasa-kamaboko — leaf-shaped fish cake (Sendai specialty)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {練|ね}り{物|もの}コーナー: fish paste products section (in a supermarket)
- {練|ね}り{物|もの}を{入|い}れる: to add fish paste products (to a dish)

USAGE:
Commonly associated with おでん (a winter stew), {鍋|なべ} (hot pot), and {弁当|べんとう} (bento boxes). Supermarkets have a dedicated {練|ね}り{物|もの} section, usually near the refrigerated fish products.
